threads_text: Anthropic renamed Claude Max 20x to Ultra and dropped the 5-hour session limit for verified accounts, at the same $200 a month. The weekly cap stays put, so this is about longer sittings, not a bigger budget. Is a $200 AI plan worth it for you?

Prices did not change. Current subscribers were moved over automatically.

Newer accounts keep a temporary limit until verified, and get an email when it is lifted.

site_article.headline: Anthropic renames Claude Max 20x to Ultra and drops its five-hour limit for verified accounts
site_article.dek: The $200 plan keeps its price and its weekly cap, while the $100 tier is now simply called Max.
site_article.summary: On October 30, 2026, Anthropic renamed its Claude Max 5x and Max 20x subscriptions to Max and Ultra, at unchanged prices of $100 and $200 a month. Verified Ultra accounts no longer have a five-hour session limit, but weekly limits stay the same.
site_article.seo_title: Claude Max 20x becomes Ultra, no 5-hour limit for verified users
site_article.seo_description: Anthropic renamed Claude Max 20x to Ultra at $200 a month and removed its five-hour limit for verified accounts. Weekly limits did not change.
site_article.answer_summary: Yes, Claude's $200 plan, now called Ultra, no longer has a five-hour session limit for verified accounts as of October 30, 2026. Its weekly usage limit is unchanged, and newer accounts keep a temporary five-hour limit until they are verified.
site_article.hero_alt: A developer stepping through a hole in a brick wall with an orange Claude logo above it.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic renamed its two Claude Max subscriptions on October 30, 2026, and removed the five-hour session limit from the top tier for verified accounts. In a post on the official Claude account on X, the company said the $100 Max 5x plan is now called Max and the $200 Max 20x plan is now called Ultra, with prices unchanged, according to FourWeekMBA.

Anthropic said it is removing the five-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts, starting that day with most existing subscribers, and that weekly limits remain unchanged, FourWeekMBA and Data Studios report. Existing subscribers were moved to the new plan names automatically and do not need to cancel or sign up again.

The updated Claude pricing page, as read by FourWeekMBA shortly after the announcement, describes Max as offering five times Pro usage every five hours and every week. The Ultra card lists no five-hour limit and ten times Pro usage every week, with a footnote saying the five-hour limit is lifted only for verified accounts.

Monthly Claude API credits also differ by tier, according to FourWeekMBA and Data Studios: $200 a month on Ultra and $100 on Max. Data Studios reports that these credits apply to a linked Console organization, cannot be used for interactive Claude Code sessions or extra usage in the Claude apps, and do not roll over.

Ultra still has limits. Data Studios and Superpower Daily report that it carries a weekly limit across all models and a separate weekly cap for Fable models, and that Anthropic may add further limits on specific models or features to manage capacity. Superpower Daily adds that Ultra is a plan for individuals, not Team or Enterprise customers, and that the $200 figure applies to web billing, with mobile prices able to differ.
The Pro plan is unchanged at $20 a month, or $17 a month billed annually, and keeps both its five-hour and weekly limits, Data Studios reports.

Newer accounts keep a temporary five-hour limit until they are verified and receive an email when it is removed, Anthropic said, describing the step as a way to prevent fraud and abuse, according to FourWeekMBA. Data Studios and Superpower Daily report that verification happens automatically based on signals such as account and payment history, and that entering a phone number at checkout does not remove the limit on its own.

Data Studios reports that subscribers can check their status under Settings and Usage, where a verified Ultra account no longer shows the current session bar. FourWeekMBA notes that Anthropic has not explained how many Ultra subscribers are already verified or how long newer accounts will wait.

The change follows reports that Anthropic had been adjusting Max 20x limits. FourWeekMBA and CellCog cite SemiAnalysis measurements from late October that found one tested account with a five-hour window about 19 percent larger and a weekly budget about 20 percent smaller.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the rename makes the plan names describe the weekly budget more honestly, since the old 20x label pointed at the five-hour window while the new Ultra card lists 10x Pro per week. For heavy users who run long coding or research sessions, the practical gain is fewer forced pauses inside a day, not more total usage across a week.
The next thing to watch is how quickly newer Ultra subscribers clear verification, and whether Anthropic publishes the criteria or extends the same treatment to the $100 Max plan.
